title.narrative: Strengthened capacity to compile, analyse and disseminate information on conditions in the labour market in Suriname

description.narrative:
Suriname, a high-middle income country, faces economic challenges that have undermined decent work prospects. With a labour force participation rate of 54%, youth unemployment is high, particularly among young women. The Suriname Decent Work Country Program (DWCP) 2023-2026 aims to address these issues, focusing on skills development through the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) system. Despite advancements, there is a need to enhance work-based training quality, provide staff capacity building, and align training programs with labour market demands.
The DWCP's strategy involves creating an action plan, resourcing strategy, and monitoring framework to facilitate job creation, especially for marginalized groups. The program will support the reform of public employment services and strengthen TVET policies. Capacity building will focus on adopting a work-based framework based on the ILO Quality Apprenticeship model, with pilot training in rural areas targeting minorities and promoting the enrolment of young women. This initiative aims to improve job prospects and economic resilience in Suriname.
